newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up as interim season starts.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up as interim season starts.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares rose two percent on Monday as foreign institutions began cautiously re-entering the market to buy at the start of the reporting season for interim results, brokers said.
Sentiment was helped after plush material maker Shanghai Haixin Co on Monday became the first company to post its results for the first half of 1997, announcing a 75 percent rise in net profit.
The B index ended the day up 1.522 points or 2.01 percent to 77.373 points on volume of 9.045 million shares worth $5.545 million.
Haixin's net profit reached 45.876 million yuan based on domestic accounting standards for the half-year ended June 30, the company said.

Although Haixin is not a heavyweight in the B share market, the note of optimism gave investors an excuse to buy, brokers said. Foreign institutions were seen picking up shares of other companies expected to post good results, they said.
"Everyone took Haixin's results as a reason to enter the market," said an analyst at an Asian securities firm. "Foreign institutions bought selectively with an eye towards interim results."
Haixin was suspended from trading on Monday morning, but ended the day up $0.034 or 5.76 percent to $0.624 as one of the day's top gainers.
Listed companies are required to report interim results by the end of August, and companies that perform poorly typically wait until shortly before the deadline to announce.
Despite the rise on Monday, the index failed to close above 78 points after reaching a high of 78.094 earlier in the day, indicating technical resistance at higher levels, brokers said.
Of 45 B shares, 42 traded with 24 up, eight flat and 10 down.
Shanghai Steel Tube Co was the star B share in the rising market, surging $0.010 or 8.33 percent to $0.130.
Recently-listed Hainan Airlines Co was the most actively traded B share on domestic buying. It rose $0.014 or 2.70 percent to $0.532 on volume of around 2.5 million shares.
Meanwhile, Shanghai's domestic currency A share index added to gains from Friday but investors remained wary, awaiting signs the market was headed decisively higher, brokers said.
The A index closed up 32.403 points or 2.68 percent to 1,239.260 points on volume of 533.578 million shares worth 6.476 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 94.045 points or 2.48 percent to end the day at 3,888.107 points.
Brokers said both the A and B share markets were likely to test higher on Tuesday with interim results providing direction in the short term.
"Further direction will depend on market-moving factors such as interim results," one local broker said.
